subject: WTA (Women's Tennis Association)
query: what does WTA stand for in tennis
title: What does WTA stand for in tennis? The women's tour explained
answer: WTA stands for Women's Tennis Association, the organization that runs the main professional tour for women's tennis and publishes the official world rankings. Billie Jean King founded it in 1973. The men's counterpart is the ATP, the Association of Tennis Professionals.
body:
The WTA was created in June 1973 at a meeting of more than 60 players in London, the week before Wimbledon. Billie Jean King led the effort to give women players one organization to bargain for equal treatment and prize money. Today the WTA represents about 1,600 players and runs tournaments on six continents. Its season ends with the WTA Finals, which brings together the year's top eight singles players and top eight doubles teams.

The WTA Tour has four levels of events, named for the ranking points a champion earns: WTA 1000, WTA 500, WTA 250 and WTA 125. The four Grand Slams (the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open) are not WTA events, but they award the most ranking points, 2,000 to the singles champion.

The official rankings, now called the PIF WTA Rankings, cover a rolling 52 weeks. A player's singles ranking adds up her best 18 results: the four Grand Slams, her best six results at the seven biggest WTA 1000 events (Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid, Rome, Canada, Cincinnati and Beijing), her best result at one of the three smaller 1000 events (Doha, Dubai and Wuhan), and her next seven best results. Points from the WTA Finals count as a 19th event. Doubles rankings use a player's best 12 results.

faq.a: The series of professional women's tournaments run by the Women's Tennis Association, with events ranked WTA 1000, 500, 250 and 125, plus the season-ending WTA Finals.
Billie Jean King, at a meeting of more than 60 players in London in June 1973.

faq.q: What is the difference between the WTA and the ATP?
faq.a: The WTA runs the women's professional tour, and the ATP runs the men's tour. Each publishes its own world rankings.

faq.q: Are Grand Slams part of the WTA?
faq.a: No. The Grand Slams are run separately, but they count toward WTA rankings and give the most points, 2,000 to the winner.

faq.q: How many points does a WTA 1000 winner get?
faq.a: 1,000. A WTA 500 champion gets 500, a WTA 250 champion 250 and a WTA 125 champion 125.
They add up a player's best 18 singles results over the past 52 weeks, including the four Grand Slams, with the WTA Finals counting as a 19th event.
